Title: Captured-corpus native building mesh allocation and scene retention

Sources.MetadataNote: Renderer binaries were frozen before candidate API commit creation; every changed source/test file was independently checked against the published candidate tree. Final reports explicitly identify9171e95 orc937ddd. Earlier scratch-only reports were preserved and are not silently relabeled.

Scope: Native x64 structural/allocation accounting, not a timing benchmark or WebAssembly heap-occupancy measurement.

The captured-only union contains68 external z14 vector tiles and96 DEM tiles. It excludes the nine bundled Manhattan vectors and z0 DEM because those did not make provider HTTP requests. All captured vectors are supplied simultaneously; this is not a proven current Display membership or tile-publication timeline.

The five fixed-p2 poses are derived diagnostic views, including look176.4 degrees. They are not the actual captured look133.2-degree gesture or its adaptive p2/p3/p4 sequence. The browser regression independently replays that interaction/corpus.

Constructor allocated bytes include tessellation, compact staging, final arrays and equal reflection overhead. TileGeometry/native-path creation and diagnostic accounting are outside each measured constructor interval.
Full-GC checkpoints intentionally measure retention and alter allocation/lifetime scheduling. Two immutable frames are retained in the scene mode; no GL context is created.

Tracked managed array payloads deduplicate references, exclude array/object headers and uncounted managed graphs, and exclude separately reported depth workspaces. Native raster image bytes describe pixel payload only.

SKPath point/verb counts are exact. Their linear payload figures are logical counts, not exact unique native allocation or raster-edge expansion. Candidate merged-shadow inputs include cached blocks and precede stroke/dash expansion.
mallinfo2 is process-wide libc allocation, not Skia-only allocation. Do not add these figures to RSS or GC committed bytes. Native x64 sizes/allocator/Skia differ from wasm32.

This demonstrates lower native managed allocation and retention while preserving the tested outputs. It does not itself identify the exact allocation size or prove the cause of the earlier native abort.
